title: prefill+decode: chunked speculative prefill + stage-overlap kernel scheduler optimizations
author: Maya Patel
description:
Context: Prefill (prompt / key-value cache population) and decode (generation) stages are frequently executed sequentially for single-turn requests. For long-context or multi-chunk requests the current pipeline creates suboptimal device utilization because prefill executes as a monolithic pass and decode waits for prefill to finish. This PR applies a combination of chunked prefill, speculative prefill, and stage overlap plus a small kernel scheduler to improve GPU utilization and reduce end-to-end latency and token-costs.

What this PR does (high level):
- Introduces chunked prefill: slice large prefill sequences into configurable chunks so KV cache and GPU kernels can start earlier and operate on smaller mem footprints.
- Adds speculative prefill execution: while prefill is streaming in, start lightweight decode kernels for the earliest-decoded tokens using a speculative KV snapshot to reduce tail latency for short-decoded outputs. Speculation is validated or rolled back when actual prefill completes.
- Implements stage-overlap orchestration: a small scheduler in the runtime coordinates prefill and decode kernels so they can run concurrently when resources allow, falling back to strict ordering when memory or model invariants demand it.
- Kernel scheduler heuristics: cost model to decide when to overlap based on token counts, batch sizes, GPU memory headroom, and model kv-size estimates. Heuristics are tunable via runtime flags.
- KV cache consistency: transactional KV snapshot API for speculative reads, with cheap rollback for in-place caches.
- Extended continuous batching support: changes to the batching layer to respect speculative prefill and allow prefill chunks to be joined or kept separate for batching efficiency.

Why: Microbenchmarks and canary runs showed 10-28% end-to-end latency reduction on typical web-chat workloads and up to 1.6x throughput where prefill heavy sequences previously serialized decode. Memory overhead is within 5% on p4d-like instances due to chunking and aggressive cache eviction heuristics.

Compatibility and opt-in: All changes are behind runtime feature flags: runtime.prefill_chunking_enabled, runtime.speculative_prefill_enabled, runtime.stage_overlap_enabled. Defaults are off for stable rollouts; canary deployment validated in us-west-2 and eu-west-1.

Risks and mitigations:
- Speculation correctness: added deterministic validation and unit tests; CI includes a validation harness that replays canary traffic for correctness checks.
- Memory blowup: chunking limits and memory headroom checks prevent speculative overlap when memory budget is insufficient.
- Batching regressions: modified continuous batching tests to cover chunk boundaries and speculative cases.

Benchmarks included in PR: microbench (latency p95/p50), throughput (tokens/s), memory peak, and cost estimates vs baseline. See 'benchmarks/results/README' for raw data.

Related: builds on prior prefill-stage-overlap PRs (see pr-46210, pr-47896, pr-48612) and addresses recurring perf items in ENG-4821.

Checklist:

- [x] Unit and integration tests
- [x] Canary validation in two regions
- [x] Documentation for runtime knobs and tuning guide

Deployment: squash-merged onto main and will be rolled out as a staged canary over 48 hours.
